title: Fixed Deposits (FD) vs Recurring Deposits (RD) & DICGC Insurance
questions: What is the difference between FD and RD?
How safe are bank fixed deposits in India?
What is DICGC deposit insurance limit?
How much TDS is deducted on FD interest?
content: Term deposits provide guaranteed returns for fixed tenures: (1) Fixed Deposit (FD): Lump-sum deposit locked for a specific duration (7 days to 10 years) at a fixed interest rate. Premature withdrawals incur a penal rate deduction (typically 0.5% to 1.0%). (2) Recurring Deposit (RD): Regular monthly savings scheme where a fixed sum is deposited every month for a chosen tenure. (3) DICGC Insurance Cover: Under the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) Act, all depositor funds (principal plus accrued interest across savings, current, FD, and RD) are insured up to ₹5,00,000 per depositor per bank in case of bank liquidation or moratorium. (4) Tax Deducted at Source (TDS): Banks deduct 10% TDS if annual interest exceeds ₹40,000 (₹50,000 for senior citizens). Submit Form 15G/15H to prevent TDS if total income is below taxable limits.
source: DICGC Act 1961 & RBI Master Direction on Interest Rates on Deposits

title: DICGC ₹5 Lakh Insurance Cover: Per Depositor, Per Bank Protection
questions: How does the ₹5 Lakh DICGC insurance work across multiple branches of the same bank?
Can I protect more than ₹5 Lakh by opening accounts in different capacities?
How quickly does DICGC pay depositors if a bank collapses?
Are fixed deposits in small finance banks covered by DICGC?
content: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC), a wholly owned subsidiary of RBI, provides statutory protection for bank deposits: (1) Coverage Cap: Insures principal and interest up to a maximum of ₹5 Lakh per depositor per insured bank. All branches of the same bank are aggregated together for this ₹5 Lakh calculation. (2) Different Capacities Strategy: Separate ₹5 Lakh limits apply to accounts held in genuinely different capacities (e.g. ₹5 Lakh for Individual Account, plus ₹5 Lakh for Joint Account with spouse where primary order is reversed, plus ₹5 Lakh for Sole Proprietorship). (3) Mandatory 90-Day Payout: Under the 2021 DICGC Amendment, depositors of banks placed under RBI moratorium must receive insurance payouts within 90 days. Covers all commercial, small finance, and cooperative banks.
source: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) Act & Guidelines

title: Fixed Deposit Premature Withdrawal Penalties & Step-Down Rates
questions: What is the penalty for breaking a fixed deposit early?
How do banks calculate interest on premature FD withdrawal?
Can I withdraw my fixed deposit before maturity online?
Is there any FD that cannot be withdrawn prematurely?
content: Withdrawing an FD before its maturity date incurs interest recalculations: (1) Calculation Method: The interest paid is NOT the original contracted rate. The bank pays the interest rate applicable for the actual period the deposit remained with the bank (broken tenure rate), MINUS a premature withdrawal penalty (typically 0.50% to 1.00%). (2) Example: If you booked a 5-year FD at 7.5% but withdraw after 1 year (where the 1-year rate is 6.0%), with a 1% penalty, the bank pays only 5.0% (6.0% - 1.0%). (3) Non-Callable FDs: Deposits without premature withdrawal options (offered for deposits ≥ ₹1 Crore or specialized retail schemes) pay slightly higher interest but cannot be broken.
source: RBI Master Direction - Interest Rate on Deposits

title: Senior Citizen FD Rates: 0.50% Extra Interest & Super Senior Schemes
questions: How much extra interest do senior citizens get on fixed deposits?
What is a super senior citizen FD rate in India?
What proof is needed to get senior citizen FD rates?
Does the senior citizen interest rate apply to joint FDs?
content: Banks offer preferential interest margins for older citizens: (1) Senior Citizens (Age 60 to 79): Receive a standard 0.50% (50 basis points) higher interest rate over standard public rates across all tenure brackets. (2) Super Senior Citizens (Age 80 and above): Several commercial and public sector banks provide an additional 0.25% to 0.30% (total 0.75% to 0.80% extra margin). (3) Joint Accounts Rule: To avail of senior citizen interest rates on a joint FD, the primary/first account holder must be a senior citizen. Age proof is verified once via Aadhaar, PAN, or Passport.
source: RBI Master Direction - Interest Rate on Deposits & Bank Schedules

title: 5-Year Tax Saver Fixed Deposits under Section 80C: Lock-in & Taxability
questions: How much tax can I save with a 5-year tax saver FD?
Can I break a tax saver FD before 5 years?
Can I take a loan against a tax-saving fixed deposit?
Is the interest earned on tax-saver FDs tax-free?
content: Specialized fixed deposits notified under the Bank Term Deposit Scheme 2006: (1) Section 80C Deduction: Investment up to ₹1,50,000 per financial year qualifies for tax deduction under Section 80C (Old Tax Regime). (2) Strict 5-Year Lock-In: The deposit cannot be prematurely withdrawn, liquidated, or closed under any circumstances before completing 5 full years. (3) No Pledging or Loans: Tax-saver FDs cannot be pledged as collateral or used to obtain overdrafts or bank loans. (4) Interest is Fully Taxable: While the principal earns a tax deduction, all interest earned is fully taxable under the depositor's applicable income-tax slab, and subject to TDS.
source: Bank Term Deposit Scheme 2006 & Income Tax Act Section 80C

title: TDS on Fixed Deposit Interest: Section 194A, Form 15G and Form 15H Rules
questions: What is the difference between Form 15G and Form 15H?
When does a bank deduct TDS on fixed deposit interest?
What is the threshold for TDS on FD interest in India?
How do I stop bank from deducting TDS on my FD?
content: Section 194A of the Income Tax Act mandates Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on bank interest: (1) Statutory Thresholds: Banks deduct 10% TDS if total interest across all branches of that bank exceeds ₹40,000 in a financial year for general citizens (₹50,000 for senior citizens). If PAN is not provided, TDS is deducted at 20%. (2) Form 15G: Self-declaration submitted by individuals aged below 60 whose total estimated income is below the basic tax exemption limit, requesting the bank not to deduct TDS. (3) Form 15H: Self-declaration submitted by senior citizens (aged 60+) whose net tax liability is zero. Both forms must be submitted fresh at the start of each financial year (April).
source: Income Tax Act 1961 Section 194A & CBDT Notifications

title: Cumulative (Reinvestment) vs Non-Cumulative (Payout) Fixed Deposits
questions: What is the difference between cumulative and non-cumulative fixed deposit?
Which gives higher returns: cumulative or non-cumulative FD?
How is interest compounded in bank fixed deposits in India?
Can I get monthly pension-like income from fixed deposits?
content: Banks offer two payout structures for term deposits: (1) Cumulative (Reinvestment) FD: Interest is compounded quarterly and reinvested alongside the principal. The entire corpus (principal + accumulated interest) is paid out in a lump-sum at maturity. Results in higher effective annual yields due to the power of quarterly compounding. (2) Non-Cumulative (Payout) FD: Interest is not reinvested; instead, it is disbursed into the depositor's savings account at regular intervals (monthly, quarterly, or half-yearly). Ideal for retirees and pensioners seeking predictable monthly cash flows to meet household living expenses.
source: RBI Master Direction on Interest Rates on Deposits

title: Sweep-in Fixed Deposits / Auto-Sweep: Liquidity with Higher FD Returns
questions: What is auto-sweep facility in a savings bank account?
How does a sweep-in fixed deposit work?
Does auto-sweep incur premature withdrawal penalties?
Can auto-sweep prevent cheque bounces?
content: Sweep-in / Flexi-Deposit facilities bridge the gap between liquid savings accounts and higher-yielding FDs: (1) Auto-Sweep Mechanism: When the savings account balance crosses a pre-set threshold (e.g. ₹25,000), surplus funds automatically transfer in multiples of e.g. ₹5,000 into short-term FDs earning higher FD interest rates. (2) Reverse Sweep on Demand: When a cheque, ATM withdrawal, or UPI debit exceeds the liquid savings balance, the bank automatically 'reverse-sweeps' the exact deficit from the linked FD units using LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) logic, preventing transaction failure without disturbing the remaining FD units.
source: RBI Guidelines on Value-Added Retail Deposit Products

title: Loan and Overdraft Against Fixed Deposit: Interest Spread & Repayment
questions: Can I get a loan against my fixed deposit?
What is the interest rate for a loan against FD?
How much loan can I get on a ₹10 Lakh FD?
Why is loan against FD better than breaking an FD?
content: Taking a loan or overdraft (OD) against an FD enables urgent liquidity without breaking the deposit: (1) Loan Quantum: Banks sanction up to 85% to 95% of the total FD principal and accrued interest value as a secured overdraft limit. (2) Interest Spread: The interest charged is typically only 1.0% to 2.0% above the FD interest rate (e.g. if the FD earns 7.0%, the loan interest is 8.0% to 9.0%). (3) Key Advantages: No processing fees, no credit score / CIBIL checks, and interest is charged strictly on the amount utilized for the exact number of days borrowed, while the underlying FD continues to earn full interest undisturbed.
source: RBI Master Direction on Advances Against Fixed Deposits

title: Recurring Deposit (RD) Mechanics: Monthly Compounding & Default Penalties
questions: What happens if I miss a monthly recurring deposit payment?
How is recurring deposit interest compounded?
Can I change my monthly RD instalment amount?
How much penalty is charged for late RD payments?
content: Recurring Deposits (RDs) inculcate disciplined monthly savings: (1) Operational Structure: A fixed agreed amount (e.g. ₹1,000, ₹5,000) is debited automatically every month for a chosen tenure (6 months to 10 years) at a guaranteed interest rate. (2) Compounding: Under Indian banking conventions, RD interest is compounded quarterly. (3) Late Payment Penalty: If an instalment is not paid by the due date, banks levy a small delay fee (typically ₹1.50 to ₹2.00 per ₹100 of instalment per month). (4) Account Discontinuation: If consecutive instalments (typically 4 or 6 months) remain unpaid, the bank reserves the right to close the RD prematurely, crediting proceeds to the savings account.
source: Indian Banks' Association (IBA) Model Rules on Recurring Deposits & RBI Norms

title: NRI Bank Deposits: NRE vs NRO vs FCNR Fixed Deposits & Repatriation
questions: What is the difference between NRE, NRO, and FCNR fixed deposits?
Is NRE fixed deposit interest taxable in India?
Can I transfer money freely from an NRE account abroad?
What currency is an FCNR deposit maintained in?
content: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can hold term deposits under Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) rules: (1) NRE (Non-Resident External) FD: Maintained in Indian Rupees, funded by foreign remittances. Both principal and interest are completely tax-free in India and freely repatriable abroad. (2) NRO (Non-Resident Ordinary) FD: Maintained in Indian Rupees for legitimate income earned inside India (rent, dividends). Interest is subject to 30% TDS + surcharge, and repatriation is capped at $1 Million USD per financial year. (3) FCNR (Foreign Currency Non-Resident) FD: Maintained in major foreign currencies (USD, GBP, EUR, JPY), eliminating currency exchange risk; interest is completely tax-free in India.
source: RBI Master Direction - Remittance Facilities for Non-Resident Indians & FEMA Norms

title: Floating Rate Fixed Deposits vs Fixed Rate FDs: Interest Cycle Hedging
questions: What is a floating rate fixed deposit in India?
When should I choose a floating rate FD over a fixed rate FD?
How does a floating rate FD change with RBI repo rate?
Does floating rate FD protect against rising inflation?
content: Floating rate term deposits protect depositors during rising interest rate cycles: (1) Benchmark Linking: The interest rate on a floating rate FD is not locked; it is tied directly to an external financial benchmark, such as the RBI Repo Rate or Treasury Bill (T-Bill) yields, with a fixed spread added on top. (2) Reset Mechanics: When the RBI alters the Repo Rate in monetary policy meetings, the FD interest rate resets automatically on pre-determined quarterly reset dates. (3) Strategic Choice: Advantageous during economic phases when inflation is climbing and interest rate hikes are anticipated, but disadvantageous when central banks begin easing and lowering rates.
source: RBI Guidelines on Floating Rate Deposit Products & Benchmark Linking
